_comment: Durable snapshot of the master build plan's per-task status. The live artifact linked from DEVELOPMENT.md is the interactive authority; this file exists so the plan's state survives if that artifact becomes unavailable. Regenerate whenever task status changes materially. 'Complete' means merged to main and nothing else. 'planned_files_not_on_main' flags a Complete task whose planned file paths are absent from main - usually a harmless rename (e.g. docs/units.md shipped as docs/UNITS_CONVENTION.md) or an intentional deletion (T0-1 removed app/simulator.py), but worth checking.

status_vocabulary.In Progress: Implementation underway; code may exist on a branch
status_vocabulary.Blocked: Waiting on a dependency or decision
status_vocabulary.Ready for Review: Code complete, rebased on current main, suite green, PR open, NOT merged
status_vocabulary.Complete: Merged to main. Nothing else counts.

tasks.name: Static typing baseline
tasks.note: Establish static typing before T4 solver interfaces expand the architectural surface area. mypy 2.3.1 pinned in requirements-dev.txt, configured in pyproject.toml over app/ only (disallow_untyped_defs, disallow_any_generics, no_implicit_optional, warn_return_any, strict_equality). All of app/ is typed and the check is clean; app/config.py is deliberately unannotated because its constants infer exactly, and tests/ are outside the scope. New module app/statetypes.py names the JSON-safe row every get_state() returns, so C1, C2 and C4 agree on one invariant dict type. Port.node is typed against a PortNode protocol so C1 still does not import C2. Only deliberate Any is in app/plant/validate.py, which walks decoded JSON of unknown shape. No runtime behaviour change; 202 tests green and golden traces unchanged. CLAUDE.md now carries the typing policy (replacing the no-type-hints rule), the Agent model guidance section and the Commit discipline section; DEVELOPMENT.md requires a green type check for Ready for Review and links to CLAUDE.md. Cross-cutting: held the spine lock until merged, then released it for T4-1. T18-2 (CI) should run the same check. Merged to main as 4128876cc35f42bba1cb3382a2b038901f7edac8 (Merge T0-7: Static typing baseline for production Python), 19 Sep. Full suite 202/202 green on main post-merge.

tasks.name: Golden-value regression harness
tasks.note: Merged to main as 6a1c1f6, then completed in 92286e9 (ff from test/golden-regression-pump), 18 Sep. The first merge covered the compressor only and shipped no proof the harness would fail if the numbers moved, so two of the task's own merge criteria were unmet; both are now closed. Six pump scenarios added in tests/fixtures/golden/pump_traces.json, mirroring the compressor's and chosen to pin the branches a refactor is most likely to break: discharge_header_change crosses into and back out of the dead-headed zero-flow branch, max_flow_clip lands on the max_flow clamp exactly. Replay now drives each run through the same scenario function that captured it — it previously re-derived the script by substring-matching the recorded command descriptions, so the replay could silently diverge from the run that produced the numbers it was checking. Tolerances documented with their reasoning and pinned from both sides: 1e-5 relative / 1e-7 absolute sits ten orders above double-precision noise and three below the 1% drift the harness exists to catch; tests assert a 1% injected change is caught on both devices (135 field diffs on the compressor, first at step 1, each naming the field, both values and the delta) and that 1e-9 noise is ignored. compressor_traces.json is byte-identical after regeneration, so the restructure moved nothing already locked. Full suite 74 green. Pushed to origin/main.

tasks.name: Equipment base class and Port
tasks.note: Merged to main as c82436d + 22066fa (ff from refactor/equipment-contract), 18 Sep, and pushed to origin/main. Branch deleted. Checkpoint A reached — C1 is frozen. Review found the branch carried a duplicate of T0-2 (55bd80d re-added the url_for fix and both redirect tests, already on main as 7742609); rebased onto main dropping it, so the merge is purely additive: app/equipment/base.py + tests/test_equipment_contract.py, nothing else touched. Added one fix during review (22066fa): Port now has __slots__, because the docstring and C1 both claim there is nowhere on a port to put a pressure or a flow, but Port was a plain object — the claim was a convention, not a guarantee. Full suite 63 green at merge (74 after T1-1 completion). Two things for the spine owner, deliberately NOT changed since C1 freezes here: (1) every contract test constructs device_class() with no arguments, so zero-arg construction is now implicitly part of C1 and each device must hard-code a default tag — that collides with T1-5, where the registry is meant to own tags; resolve it as its own task rather than as a side effect. (2) REGISTERED is computed at test-module import time, so an Equipment subclass defined in a module imported later silently escapes the parameterised contract tests. Also note the contract tests currently parameterise over the two test doubles only (Machine, Valve) — GasCompressor and CentrifugalPump do not subclass Equipment until T1-3/T1-4, at which point the DEVICE_MODULES import hook pulls them in automatically.

tasks.name: Refactor the compressor onto the contract
tasks.note: Merged to main as a416ff6 (fast-forward from refactor/compressor-onto-base), pushed to origin/main, branch deleted (local + remote). Full suite 93/93 green on main post-merge. GasCompressor now subclasses Equipment: ports suction(inlet)/discharge(outlet), integrate(dt) moves load and valve position only (no flow/pressure touch, satisfies integrate(0) no-op), characteristic(flow) publishes max(shutoff_pressure_rise*load**2 - compressor_resistance*flow**2, 0.0) as a pure function. step() stays as GasCompressor's own method (calls integrate(dt) then _calculate_operating_point()) since no plant-wide solver exists yet to drive devices externally — that's still M4 (T4-2). supply_pressure/discharge_header_pressure renamed to upstream_boundary_pressure/downstream_boundary_pressure so a fresh device has no attribute matching NODE_PRESSURE_ATTRIBUTES in the contract test; _calculate_operating_point's available_pressure_rise is now derived from characteristic(0.0) instead of duplicating the shutoff/load term, and the duplicate _move_toward static method is dropped in favor of Equipment's. Default tag is 'K-101', matching T1-2's note that zero-arg construction is implicitly part of C1 — same collision with T1-5's registry ownership of tags applies here too, not resolved as part of this task. Updated tests/test_compressor.py's two boundary-pressure lines and the two compressor scenario functions in tests/golden_regression.py (pump scenarios left for T1-4) to the new attribute names. Golden traces reproduce exactly; regenerating them changed only the two recorded command-description strings that named the old attributes (compressor_traces.json), pump_traces.json byte-identical. Heads up for T1-4 review: GasCompressor kept its own step()/operating-point solve (no plant-wide solver exists yet); a concurrent pump refactor observed in progress appeared to drop step() and the self-solve entirely — worth reconciling the two approaches so satellites depending on Equipment devices can assume one consistent shape.

tasks.name: Refactor the pump onto the contract
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 5e1a9f0512d9474f04b3fe3a69a252f983eb8415 (no-ff merge commit of PR #1, from refactor/pump-onto-base @ 4751cc1), 19 Sep. Full suite 202/202 green on main post-merge.

CentrifugalPump is now on the C1 Equipment contract: tag 'P-101', suction(inlet)/discharge(outlet) ports, integrate(dt) owns slow-state speed ramping only, characteristic(flow) is a pure published curve. Renamed supply_pressure/discharge_header_pressure -> upstream_boundary_pressure/downstream_boundary_pressure so no device attribute matches the contract's forbidden node-pressure names. get_state() shape unchanged, so main.py, templates/pump.html, static/pump.js, test_pump_api.py and test_pump.py needed zero changes. Golden trace values are numerically unchanged — only two recorded command-description strings naming the old attributes moved.

The pump now works through Engine: Engine.step() drives it via integrate() and Snapshot publishes its state generically by tag, with no pump-specific code in Engine/Snapshot. Closed the coverage gap T2-3 documented ('Pump coverage belongs here once T1-4 merges') by adding test_pump_golden_slow_state_reproduces_through_the_engine to tests/test_engine.py, mirroring the compressor version. CentrifugalPump is also picked up automatically by the parametrized C1 contract tests and the registry round-trip test (+7 tests on merge; 194 -> 201, +1 new engine golden test = 202).

INTENTIONALLY TEMPORARY, do not 'clean up' as a side effect of another task: both GasCompressor and CentrifugalPump retain their own step() plus _calculate_operating_point() standalone solve, and the Flask routes still call that legacy path. T4-2 (network solver) is the task that retires equipment-owned operating-point solving and the interim upstream/downstream_boundary_pressure attributes. Until then Engine deliberately calls integrate() only and does not compute flow/pressure.

Rebase history: originally branched from 63b1a0a (pre T1-3/T1-5/T2-3/T3-1/T3-2); rebased cleanly onto current main with zero conflicts before merge, since the branch only ever touched pump.py, golden_regression.py and the pump golden fixture.

tasks.name: Equipment registry and tag naming
tasks.note: Merged to main as 5ea07cb, pushed to origin/main. Branch feature/equipment-registry deleted locally (was never pushed to origin, so no remote delete needed). Full suite green (98 tracked tests at merge time: 93 pre-existing + 5 new). EquipmentRegistry (app/equipment/registry.py) maps tag -> device instance: register() raises ValueError naming the device already holding a tag instead of silently overwriting it, resolve() raises KeyError naming the missing tag plus every tag that is registered. app/config.py gets an appended TAG_PREFIXES section documenting the ISA-style convention (K/P/E/V/FV) referenced from the registry's docstring. tests/test_registry.py round-trips every class currently in Equipment.registered() (same DEVICE_MODULES/dynamic-discovery idiom as test_equipment_contract.py, so it automatically picks up CentrifugalPump once T1-4 lands) plus duplicate/unknown-tag cases. Not wired into app/main.py or any Plant object yet — that's for whichever later task actually builds a Plant from config (T3-3) or gives sessions their own registry (T2-4); T1-5 only builds the mechanism. Process note, not a code issue: while committing, this shared working tree's checked-out branch got switched out from under me mid-task (another session created feature/plant-config-schema fresh off main between my `checkout -b` and `commit`), so my first commit attempt (d41949a) landed on THAT branch instead of mine. I cherry-picked it onto the correct feature/equipment-registry branch (now merged as 5ea07cb) but could not clean up the stray d41949a on feature/plant-config-schema — the sandbox blocked both `reset --hard` and `git revert` on that branch as cross-workload interference, correctly, since another session owns it. By the time I could react, that session had already committed T3-1 on top of it and pushed (5b2ad19). See the note on T3-1 for what that means for their branch.

tasks.name: Seeded RNG service
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 26748e7 (PR #9). The earlier claim of a merge at 611c5b6 was false: that commit was local-only, never pushed, and is superseded. This is a rewrite, not a rebase: the draft failed mypy (6 errors), had no lint test, and its independence test would pass with shared state. app/engine/rng.py: SeededRNG (typed; a seed is required, since an unseeded generator is nondeterministic) with random/uniform/gauss/randint/choice/shuffle and reseed(). tests/test_rng.py (10) covers determinism of every draw method, reseed, and stream independence (interleaving draws from a second stream leaves the first bit-identical to drawing it alone). tests/test_random_source_guard.py (21) fails if any app/ module other than rng.py imports random; verified it catches a stray import. Full suite 297 passed, mypy clean.

DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED: a module-level global RNG with set_seed()/uniform() free functions (present in the old draft). A process-wide stream would be shared by every browser session, and SessionRegistry gives each session its own plant, so two sessions would see each other's draws and break the same-config/same-seed/same-steps determinism rule. Which object owns a plant's RNG (per session, per engine, or per plant) is an open design decision for the first task that needs randomness; nothing in app/ draws random numbers today.

tasks.name: Engine step loop and snapshot publisher
tasks.note: Merged to local main as 1eeb089 + 209662c (ff from refactor/simulation-engine, rebased onto origin/main's 07d4d1d worktree-docs commit — clean, no code overlap). /code-review high ran 8 finder agents in parallel; 5 independently converged on the same root cause (Engine.running was a second, unsynchronized running flag that step() never checked — stop() didn't stop anything). Fixed by deleting the flag: start()/stop() now delegate to SimulationClock.pause()/resume(), snapshot's running field reads off clock.paused. Also fixed from review: SimulationClock.step() now returns elapsed sim-time instead of Engine re-deriving it by diffing; Engine's constructor takes an iterable (not a pre-keyed dict) so equipment dict keys can't diverge from device.tag; Snapshot._frozen() now deep-copies (matching base.py's _snapshot() precedent) instead of shallow-copying; alarms entries are now deep-frozen too (previously only the outer tuple was immutable, contradicting the module's own docstring); solver=None vs explicit solver={} are now distinguished. Documented+pinned rather than fixed (would require touching satellite-owned compressor.py/pump.py, out of scope): device.simulation_speed is not consulted by Engine — a new test proves this explicitly rather than relying on both defaulting to 1.0 by coincidence. Rejected: removing the C4 placeholder sections (violates T2-3's own 'matches C4 exactly' requirement), dropping MappingProxyType immutability (contradicts Port's __slots__ precedent + breaks leak tests), and 6 efficiency suggestions (memoization/parallel-gather) that target throughput problems this 1Hz poll-driven simulator doesn't have. Full suite 130 green. NOT YET PUSHED to origin — checking with the user first since this is spine work with high blast radius (unblocks feature/plant-topology next).

tasks.name: Node, branch and stream structures
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 2e56c48 (fast-forward from feature/plant-topology, rebased onto origin/main's T2-3 first), 19 Sep. Pushed to origin/main; feature branch deleted (remote + local worktree). gh's stored PR credentials were invalid (keyring token bad), so this landed as a direct fast-forward push rather than through a GitHub PR — no GitHub PR record exists for T3-2. Full suite 168 passed on merge (131 at review, +37 from T2-3 landing on main in the interim; rebase was clean, no conflicts). Checkpoint B is now one step closer — app/plant/topology.py is released from spine claim.

C2 as implemented: Node(id, pressure, is_boundary, elevation), Branch(id, from_node, to_node, device, flow), Stream(flow, pressure, temperature, composition), plus a Topology container. Solver-owned values are read-only properties written only via set_pressure()/set_flow() — `node.pressure = 800` raises AttributeError, a boundary node refuses set_pressure() entirely, and flow is stored once on the branch's stream (Branch.flow is a property over it).

Two decisions for T3-3/T4-1/T4-2 to build against:
(1) Port binding by direction, with explicit from_port/to_port override for devices with more than one inlet or outlet (an exchanger's utility side, a vessel's vent are a second branch on the same device — duplicate-tag check is identity-based).
(2) A branch must hold a device — Branch(..., device=None) is refused; a bare line is a resistance device, not a special case.

Deliberately NOT in this task: characteristic sign convention / reverse flow (T4-1), all solvability checks — dangling port, disconnected subgraph, zero boundary pressure, duplicate config tag (T3-3's loader, where the error can name the config path). T3-3's primitives: boundary_nodes / internal_nodes, branches_from / branches_to / branches_at, unconnected_ports(), device(tag), identity-checked add_node/add_branch.

For the snapshot owner (C4): Topology.get_state() returns nodes/branches/streams as flat JSON-safe rows, streams keyed by branch id (remap freely, no identity of their own yet). describe()/str() prints the graph for debugging.

Open note carried over from review, still true: tests/test_topology.py's Equipment double (Device) lands in REGISTERED and runs through the C1 parameterised contract tests if collected before test_equipment_contract.py — passes either way, but is a live instance of the import-order gap T1-2 flagged; not fixed here since it's out of scope for C2.

tasks.name: Plant loader and topology validation
tasks.note:
Merged to main as b2656a5 (PR #7, merge commit from feature/plant-loader, rebased on the T4-1 merge). app/plant/loader.py: load_plant(config) / load_plant_file(path) validate against the C3 schema, build a Topology and return a Plant; a bad config raises one PlantConfigError listing every problem with its config path (duplicate node ids and tags, unknown node references, boundary pressure <= 0 or no boundary, disconnected subgraphs including orphan nodes, unwired ports, device types with no model yet, unknown or wrongly-typed design keys). Plant.to_config() reads design values back off the live devices, so plant -> config -> plant round-trips identically; limits/controllers/interlocks pass through untouched. Only pump and compressor have device classes, so the other C3 type enum values are rejected until their models land. tests/test_plant_loader.py: 27 tests. Full suite 266 passed, mypy clean.

Two open questions, NOT settled here and needing an owner: (1) Equipment.reset() restores the state captured at the end of __init__, and design values are applied after construction, so a reset device returns to class defaults rather than the configured design. Fixing it needs a design/configure hook on C1 (spine change, Opus decision) before T4-2/T3-4 rely on reset() for loaded plants. (2) C3 has only node_in/node_out, so a device with more than one inlet or outlet (a vessel with a vent) cannot be wired from config; it needs from_port/to_port in the schema, which T3-1 owns. Do it when the first multi-port device (T5-1) lands. Not included: YAML loading (pyyaml is not in requirements.txt; T3-4's olefins_lite.yaml needs it) and cross-checking tags referenced by limits/controllers/interlocks.

tasks.name: Branch characteristic interface
tasks.note: Sign convention for characteristic(flow) is outlet minus inlet, positive inlet to outlet, defined for every real flow including negative, and non-increasing in flow everywhere. signed_square(q)=|q|*q in app/equipment/base.py is the primitive that makes reverse flow well defined; both devices now write their quadratic term against it. Branch gains characteristic() and residual() (the branch equation T4-2 drives to zero). The max(...,0) clamp is removed from both device curves. One golden value moves: pump supply_pressure_change step 1 pump_pressure_rise 0.0 to -1.4, which agrees with the spread recorded on the same row; edited by hand, not regenerated. compressor.py and pump.py are touched beyond the listed files because reverse flow cannot be defined in base.py alone. 238 tests green, mypy clean. Spine lock released at merge. Merged to main as 57d5c8f0d142bde1914b7427e2b2dbdc97079696 (no-ff merge commit of PR #5, from feature/branch-characteristic @ 86ef7f4), 19 Sep. Full suite 238/238 green and mypy clean on main post-merge. Unblocks T7-1; T4-2 still also needs T3-3.

tasks.name: Newton-Raphson network solver
tasks.note: Merged to main as 7d05323 (PR #13). NetworkSolver in app/engine/network.py solves branch flows and internal node pressures simultaneously: one branch equation per branch (built on T4-1's Branch.residual) and one mass balance per internal node, square, Newton-Raphson with a backtracking line search under a damping cap and an iteration cap. No numerical dependency - thirty lines of Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, because the V1 train is a handful of branches. Ordering is by sorted id, so a solve is bit-reproducible whatever order the graph was assembled in. Pressure and flow residuals carry separate tolerances and are never added together. A non-converged solve writes nothing and restores the pressures it found. Nothing calls it: Engine.step(), the Flask routes, device step(), _calculate_operating_point() and the interim *_boundary_pressure attributes are all unchanged - T4-4 retires those, T4-3 owns full diagnostics. Full suite 336 passed, mypy clean, golden traces untouched. A failed solve is atomic: unless solve() returns converged and commits, pressures and flows are exactly what they were on entry, including when an exception escapes mid-iteration. One process-domain caveat is recorded as unenforced - a topology must be a single hydraulic domain and nothing enforces that, because C2/C3/NetworkSolver carry no flow-domain metadata; T3-4 and the vessel work decide the liquid/gas split.
